definitions.explanation: Severe lack of food, ranging from extreme hunger to widespread famine. Used in serious or formal contexts about food crises and deprivation.

examples.japanese: {世界|せかい}では{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{飢餓|きが}に{直面|ちょくめん}している。
examples.english: Many people around the world are facing starvation.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}によって{引|ひ}き{起|お}こされた{飢餓|きが}で、{何百万|なんびゃくまん}もの{命|いのち}が{失|うしな}われた。
examples.english: Millions of lives were lost to famine caused by war.

notes: A formal word used in news, academic, and humanitarian contexts. Common collocations include {飢餓|きが}に{苦|くる}しむ (to suffer from starvation), {飢餓|きが}に{直面|ちょくめん}する (to face famine), and {飢餓|きが}{状態|じょうたい} (state of starvation). For everyday hunger, お{腹|なか}が{空|す}いた or {空腹|くうふく} is used instead. {飢饉|ききん} (famine) refers specifically to a large-scale food crisis affecting a region.
